_comment: Canonical Sleeper DEFAULT point-calculation chart (stat-key -> weight), in Sleeper's own scoring_settings vocabulary -- the same shape sleepermetrics.scoring.rules_from(league_id) returns, but league-free. `base` holds every scoring rule EXCEPT the points-per-reception weight; that is the ONLY thing that differs between the standard scoring formats, so it is stored once per format in `rec_by_format` and merged onto `base` by sleepermetrics.scoring.default_rules(fmt). std = 0 PPR, half_ppr = 0.5, ppr = 1.0, 2qb = 1.0 (superflex is a roster-slot difference, not a scoring one, so its chart equals PPR). A TE-premium variant would add a `bonus_rec_te` key (a per-position reception boost that stacks on `rec`); no source this project reads publishes TEP ADP, so it is not included. Derived by reconciling 39 real public Sleeper leagues (modal weight per key), pass_int set to Sleeper's true default -1, cross-checked against ESPN's published standard scoring + the profootballnetwork / fantasypointcalculators / Sleeper-support references. VERIFIED: base + the std/half_ppr/ppr rec weight reproduces Sleeper's own pts_std / pts_half_ppr / pts_ppr EXACTLY for every offensive player (5008/5008 player-format-weeks over 2023-2025) and every kicker. DST keys are the documented Sleeper defaults but do NOT reproduce Sleeper's DST pts_* exactly (Sleeper scores team defense from a richer vocabulary a linear chart can't express -- same reason sleepermetrics.scoring only scores offensive lineups). Not league-specific, not a parity artifact.
